A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAMEN research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The complete material supports comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic DAG experiments, semi-synthetic IHDP experiments, Cattaneo2 treatment-effect estimates, and appendix robustness studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3 and Algorithms 1–2 replace signed, variance-normalized cross-U losses with absolute statistics divided by empirical standard deviations, revising the stated optimization criterion. The subset-search and Gumbel procedures remain; separate T/Y masks and averaging over environments already appeared in v1's appendix.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic DAG, IHDP, and Cattaneo2 coverage, including the same invariance, collider, descendant, noise, mediator, small-sample, and heterogeneity scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: Shi et al.'s IRM approach, adjustment for all covariates, and no adjustment. No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix D replaces environment-specific nuisance fitting with pooled-data fitting for ATE estimation. D.1 also adds noise to the random-graph collider equation, although Section 5.2 retains the deterministic equation. These are reported setting revisions, without evidence of reruns. Calendar-quarter environments were already specified in v1's D.3.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same mediator, absent-invariance, random-graph, semi-synthetic, small-sample, and heterogeneity analyses and their evidence. Changes to their interpretation and presentation do not introduce new robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies the first-split sample-variance estimator and standard-deviation studentization of the cross-U statistic. Experimental uncertainty reporting is unchanged: the same 20- or 100-run standard errors and Table 1's standard deviations over 100 seed initializations remain.

E6.justification: All empirical plots retain their estimates and error bars. Table 1 is identical, including RAMEN's −214.60 ± 25.20 and IRM's −182.65 ± 48.32. No result entries are added or removed; merging figures does not change their findings.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 introduce bounded outcomes and bounded test functions, revise Assumption 4.1 to use environment-specific regressions on full-graph parents, and require positivity for every minimizer. Assumption 3.1's formula now excludes all mediators, although its prose still says observed mediators. Section 4.3 replaces equality of original and kernelized losses with equivalence of their zero-loss sets, and Appendix A.2 substantially revises the proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: doubly robust ATE identification using heterogeneous environments without learning the causal graph, and empirical advantages over existing approaches.

C2.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C.1 withdraw automatic natural-direct-effect identification when mediators are included; additional mediation assumptions are now required. The assertion that mediator absence is statistically falsifiable is removed. Section 5.4 describes birth-weight reductions relative to the literature's range instead of declaring overestimation or underestimation of an unknown true effect.

D1.justification: The revision explicitly documents environment-level draws held fixed across samples, shifts to exogenous noise, treatment-group sample sizes, and the random-graph ATE's structural coefficient. The IHDP equation now includes 2T, already specified in v1's generation summary. Hyperparameters, model architectures, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Six references are removed, including Baron and Kenny, Preacher and Hayes, and Steinwart. Comparisons with classical doubly robust estimation and conditional-distribution versus conditional-mean invariance are refined. The principal research positioning and Appendix B's coverage remain.

P1.justification: Methodology subsections are retitled and locally reorganized, estimator/estimand terminology is clarified, and several explanations and cross-references are corrected. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v1's Figures 3 and 4 become two panels of v2's Figure 3. Table 1 and several previously text-wrapped figures become centered displays, including the relocated explanatory DAG and absent-invariance plot. Their underlying graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision by replacing the incorrect loss equality with zero-loss equivalence and makes causal interpretation more defensible by withdrawing automatic natural-direct-effect identification. These gains are limited by remaining inconsistencies: the new bounded-outcome requirement is not reconciled with Gaussian synthetic outcomes, and Section 5.2 and Appendix D.1 disagree about collider noise. The empirical evidence remains unchanged.
